findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no ACL are configured for this bucket, so bucket/object ACLs or policies could expose the reports data publicly.
The bucket has no logging block, so access to the stored reports cannot be audited or investigated after a compromise.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious object deletion/overwrite is unrecoverable; combined with force_destroy = true the bucket and all contents can be destroyed without safeguards.
The ledger export bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving sensitive financial exports unencrypted at rest with no KMS key control.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes of ledger exports are not recorded to the audit trail bucket.
Versioning is disabled on a bucket holding financial ledger exports, so tampering or deletion cannot be rolled back or detected.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricting public ACLs or policies for this bucket containing sensitive ledger data.
The model artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, leaving the bucket open to accidental public ACL or policy grants.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedures and endpoints stored unencrypted.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so access to operational runbooks is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource exists for this bucket, so public ACLs or bucket policies are not blocked at the account/bucket level.
The audit trail bucket itself has no logging configuration, so access to the centralized log store is untracked, allowing log tampering to go unnoticed.
The log-delivery-write ACL bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, risking public exposure of aggregated access logs.
The vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that lacks default encryption, so sensitive vendor data is stored in plaintext.
